findings.opportunity: Baseline capture builds an element identity index but bypasses it when materializing entries, performs one relationship scan per target, and traverses Element Kind constraint closure twice.
findings.impact: Reuse identity maps and one closure traversal to change repeated target lookup from quadratic scans to indexed lookup and remove redundant graph traversal.
evidence: src/core/framing/baseline.ts creates elementsById but elementTarget scans model.elements per relevant identity.
relationshipTarget scans model.relationships once per payload Relationship.
Relationship Kind constraints are seeded only after the first Element Kind closure, forcing a second closure traversal.
findings.recommendation: Build or reuse maps for all model collections, seed Relationship Kind constraints before one Element Kind closure, and materialize values directly from maps.
findings.keyDesign: Add a Relationship map keyed by relationshipIdentity, gather all direct Kind references before one worklist closure, and preserve byte-sorted arrays and shallow-cloned values.
preservationConstraints: Preserve exact relevant-context closure and complete ancestor chains.
Preserve UTF-8 byte ordering and normalized Kind constraints.
Preserve fresh, unrelated-drift, relevant-drift classifications and exact changed keys.
Do not include Contracts, Views, source paths, or excluded model data.
implementationOutline: Add relationshipsById and remove linear-scan helpers.

Run one Kind closure and materialize from maps.
